sentences.text: The hearing has been conducted through hybrid mode (physical and virtual hearing).
CM APPL. 10616/2017 (delay of 153 days)
1. The delay of 153 days in filing of the review petition is sought to be explained on the ground that their counsel was unwell.
DDA is a large land owning agency in Delhi.
It has a large panel of lawyers and legal advisors, indeed a law Department, to advise and assist it in its legal affairs and litigation before various fora.
It is surely deemed to have legal expertise and would know well the status of its cases.
Therefore, there is no ground for condoning the delay of 5 months in filing the review petition.
Each day of delay needs to be explained.

sentences.text: Despite the above, even if the Review Petition is taken up on merits, it is not maintainable for the following reasons:

This Review Petition filed by DDA seeks review of the judgment dated 06.09.2016 on the ground that land already stood acquired under section 3 of The Resettlement of Displaced Persons (Land Acquisition) Act, 1948 by way of notification dated 05.08.1949.
4.

entities.text: Resettlement of Displaced Persons (Land Acquisition) Act, 1948
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: This issue was never raised before the Division Bench when the aforesaid judgment was passed.

It clearly records that- "... 2. It is an admitted position that neither physical possession of the subject land has been taken by the land acquiring agency, nor has any compensation been paid to the petitioner..."

The Court then referred to four judgments of the Supreme Court which gave the benefit of section 24(2) of The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to persons who fall in either of the said categories.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It was never the case of the respondents i.e. neither of the DDA nor of the LAC, that physical possession had already been taken.

5. In terms of the dicta of the Supreme Court in Indore Development Authority v. Manohar Lal and Ors. 2020 SCC OnLine SC 316, to avail the benefit of section 24(2), is to be ensured that neither physical This is a digitally signed order.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority v. Manohar Lal and Ors. 2020 SCC OnLine SC 316
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 09:03:09 possession of the land was taken away from the landowner nor compensation had been received by her/him.

6. In the present case, in terms of the afore quoted paragraph 2 of the said judgement, the petitioner meets the said conjoint condition i.e. neither physical possession was taken nor was compensation received by the petitioner.
7. There is no error apparent on the record.
The ground now raised was never an issue in the writ proceedings.
8. There is no cause for reviewing the judgment.
9. Therefore, the Review Petition is dismissed.
NAJMI WAZIRI, J SUDHIR KUMAR JAIN, J MAY 16, 2023 j/sw
